### CVE-2006-1342
- Assigner: sgi | Published: 2006-03-21 | Updated: 2024-08-07 | Max CVSS: None
- CWE: n/a
- Exploit-DB 27461: Linux Kernel 2.4.x/2.5.x/2.6.x - 'Sockaddr_In.Sin_Zero' Kernel Memory Disclosure (local/linux, 2006-03-23, verified=1)

net/ipv4/af_inet.c in Linux kernel 2.4 does not clear sockaddr_in.sin_zero before returning IPv4 socket names from the (1) getsockname, (2) getpeername, and (3) accept functions, which allows local users to obtain portions of potentially sensitive memory.

### CVE-2006-2444
- Assigner: redhat | Published: 2006-05-25 | Updated: 2024-08-07 | Max CVSS: None
- CWE: n/a
- Exploit-DB 1880: Linux Kernel < 2.6.16.18 - Netfilter NAT SNMP Module Remote Denial of Service (dos/linux, 2006-06-05, verified=1)

The snmp_trap_decode function in the SNMP NAT helper for Linux kernel before 2.6.16.18 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (crash) via unspecified remote attack vectors that cause failures in snmp_trap_decode that trigger (1) frees of random memory or (2) frees of previously-freed memory (double-free) by snmp_trap_decode as well as its calling function, as demonstrated via certain test cases of the PROTOS SNMP test suite.

Affected:
- n/a / n/a: affected n/a

### CVE-2006-2451
- Assigner: redhat | Published: 2006-07-07 | Updated: 2024-08-07 | Max CVSS: None
- CWE: n/a
- Exploit-DB 2031: Linux Kernel 2.6.13 < 2.6.17.4 - 'logrotate prctl()' Local Privilege Escalation (local/linux, 2006-07-18, verified=1)
- Exploit-DB 2004: Linux Kernel 2.6.13 < 2.6.17.4 - 'sys_prctl()' Local Privilege Escalation (1) (local/linux, 2006-07-11, verified=1)
- Exploit-DB 2005: Linux Kernel 2.6.13 < 2.6.17.4 - 'sys_prctl()' Local Privilege Escalation (2) (local/linux, 2006-07-12, verified=1)
- Exploit-DB 2006: Linux Kernel 2.6.13 < 2.6.17.4 - 'sys_prctl()' Local Privilege Escalation (3) (local/linux, 2006-07-13, verified=1)
- Exploit-DB 2011: Linux Kernel 2.6.13 < 2.6.17.4 - 'sys_prctl()' Local Privilege Escalation (4) (local/linux, 2006-07-14, verified=1)

The suid_dumpable support in Linux kernel 2.6.13 up to versions before 2.6.17.4, and 2.6.16 before 2.6.16.24, allows a local user to cause a denial of service (disk consumption) and possibly gain privileges via the PR_SET_DUMPABLE argument of the prctl function and a program that causes a core dump file to be created in a directory for which the user does not have permissions.

### CVE-2006-2629
- Assigner: mitre | Published: 2006-05-27 | Updated: 2024-08-07 | Max CVSS: None
- CWE: n/a
- Exploit-DB 27925: Linux Kernel 2.6.x - Proc dentry_unused Corruption Local Denial of Service (dos/linux, 2006-05-31, verified=1)

Race condition in Linux kernel 2.6.15 to 2.6.17, when running on SMP platforms, allows local users to cause a denial of service (crash) by creating and exiting a large number of tasks, then accessing the /proc entry of a task that is exiting, which causes memory corruption that leads to a failure in the prune_dcache function or a BUG_ON error in include/linux/list.h.

### CVE-2006-3468
- Assigner: redhat | Published: 2006-07-18 | Updated: 2024-08-07 | Max CVSS: None
- CWE: n/a
- Exploit-DB 28358: Linux Kernel 2.6.17.7 - NFS and EXT3 Combination Remote Denial of Service (dos/linux, 2006-08-07, verified=1)

Linux kernel 2.6.x, when using both NFS and EXT3, allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (file system panic) via a crafted UDP packet with a V2 lookup procedure that specifies a bad file handle (inode number), which triggers an error and causes an exported directory to be remounted read-only.

### CVE-2006-4663
- Assigner: mitre | Published: 2006-09-09 | Updated: 2025-01-17 | Max CVSS: 7.8
- CWE: n/a; CWE-noinfo Not enough information
- CVSS 3.1 (CISA-ADP): 7.8 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total

The source code tar archive of the Linux kernel 2.6.16, 2.6.17.11, and possibly other versions specifies weak permissions (0666 and 0777) for certain files and directories, which might allow local users to insert Trojan horse source code that would be used during the next kernel compilation.  NOTE: another researcher disputes the vulnerability, stating that he finds "Not a single world-writable file or directory." CVE analysis as of 20060908 indicates that permissions will only be weak under certain unusual or insecure scenarios

Affected:

- Assigner: mitre | Published: 2007-02-24 | Updated: 2024-08-07 | Max CVSS: None
- CWE: n/a
- Exploit-DB 1657: Linux Kernel 2.6.x - 'sys_timer_create()' Local Denial of Service (dos/linux, 2006-04-09, verified=1)

The sys_timer_create function in posix-timers.c for Linux kernel 2.6.x allows local users to cause a denial of service (memory consumption) and possibly bypass memory limits or cause other processes to be killed by creating a large number of posix timers, which are allocated in kernel memory but are not treated as part of the process' memory.
